chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Returning to the hotel job; Canadians bringing cakes and pies
summary: After the hospital he went back to the same Phillipsburg hotel, where locals visited, baked for him and followed his career on Montreal radio.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Was that the closest hospital? Is that where --
Yeah, that's where it happened, right outside of S[scribble], Albans. But --
You weren't into Canada yet.
No, no. We was on our way. Uh-huh.
I see. Well, when you came out of the hospital, Herman, how long was it before you could work?

Well, when I came out of the hospital I went back to Canada, which is just across the border about seven miles, on route seven, seven miles? More than that. I'm thinking about route seven. But -- okay, 18, 20 miles, maybe from -- maybe, or 30 miles. Anyway, which is nothing in a car. And I went over there and went to work. Now they had to take me --
Went to work where, in Phillipsburg?
Back at the hotel, yeah. That's where I was on my way.

Well -- now this was not like the thing you were telling me before, about the Neverly, where you were in the hospital for a month, and you don't have a job any more, but this -- you were here seven months in the hospital, and you go back, and you've still got a --
Yeh, well the drummer and the piano player were still working there. Who else was -- who was my
replacement? I think it was a tenor saxophone player, I think, as far as horn. It was only a trio.
Uh-huh, but you did get the job back.

Oh yeah, well they kept working, and they would come to see me, and all the people around there, it was like a home thing. Once you meet those people they -- they will love you for life, and they're -- and it was so nice being there, because they would cook pies, and cakes .
Really?
Yeah, different -- little kids come up and say, Mr. Herman? I'd say what? My aunt sent this over. She thought you'd like it. like it! You know, and that --
How did these people know you so well?

Well, because I worked at the hotel, and they came in on weekends, or whatnot, to dance, for different reasons, and they met me, and they liked -- liked my playing, and a lot of them had heard that I'd been with Fats, and whatnot, and this that and the other, and at that time Montreal -- uh, radio, had it, and they would record -- I mean thing every day --
Broadcast?

Yeah, broadcast it every day that Herman Autrey's here, and he did this, and here's some records he made, and this that and the other, and then a lot of people who didn't know me before would know me now.
I see.

You know. And they came down, and that's how they know, and then they started -- and then they heard about me writing a gun, or write this, or write that, blah, blah, blah, they became very much interested, and they would come in with a cake, pie, this, can I do anything for You? Anything, and they'd bring cigarettes. You know. And I would -- I became -- to know you know, I knew a heck of a lot of people.
